summary: The agent implemented most of the multiframe feature and passed the baseline suite, but five deterministic new tests fail in dimension-macro preservation and nested sequence validation.

details.reasoning: junit_base.xml reports 2,632 baseline tests with no failures or errors. junit_new.xml reports 361 new tests with five failures and no errors. Three failures arise because the derivation path removes an entire empty FrameContentSequence while pruning DimensionIndexValues, and one also removes existing index values when no DimensionIndexSequence is present. The remaining failure arises because _parse_functional_group_item rejects a nested sequence with more than one item, although only the shared functional-groups sequence has the stated one-item cardinality requirement.
details.secondary_factors: The agent's full-suite validation also encountered an unrelated TLS certificate-bundle failure while downloading external test data, but the targeted tests and the verifier's baseline/new runs completed without that issue.

quick_failure_summary: Five new tests fail because derivation deletes empty frame-content macros or values and validation rejects a valid multi-item macro sequence.

justification.issue_description: Derived instances do not preserve an empty FrameContentSequence after dimension values are removed, and the validator over-restricts nested functional-group macro sequences to one item.
justification.evidence: The prompt says that a dimension is dropped from the dimension description and from the relevant frames, that a dimension not reached by every frame is kept, and that equal macros are then stored once in the shared group; it separately specifies one-item cardinality only for a present shared group sequence. In the patch, _remove_attribute deletes the containing macro when its item becomes empty, _adjust_dimensions removes DimensionIndexValues when the description is absent, and _parse_functional_group_item raises whenever len(values) != 1. The reference implementation deletes only the DimensionIndexValues element and iterates all items of a macro sequence.
justification.verdict_reasoning: The implementation is functional and passes 356 of 361 new tests, so this is not an integration or syntax failure. The failing behaviors follow directly from the requested dimension and macro-sharing rules and from over-validating a condition that the prompt scopes to the shared functional-groups sequence. These are implementation gaps in explicitly required or foreseeable edge cases, so FAIL_MISSED_REQUIREMENT is the appropriate primary verdict rather than a test-mismatch or environment verdict.

problem_assessment.notes: This is a substantial but solvable task covering validation, functional-group derivation, dimensions, pixel encodings, provenance, isolation, grouping, and sorting. The verifier's 361 local tests are deterministic and the expectations are consistent with the prompt and reference behavior.

evidence: junit_base.xml records 2,632 tests with failures=0 and errors=0.
junit_new.xml records 361 tests with 5 failures and errors=0; each failure is an assertion or MultiFrameError reached through src/pydicom/multiframe.py, not test bootstrap.
test_execution.log reports baseline_passed=True (2632/2632) and new_tests_passed=False (356/361); the hidden test run completed in 2.49 seconds.

The trajectory shows a later full-suite run stopping at test_data_manager.py::test_fetch_data_files because certifi/cacert.pem was unavailable after 682 passed. The agent did not repeatedly debug or modify shared test setup, and this network-dependent test is excluded by the verifier wrapper.
environment_assessment.finding: The verifier is functioning and exposes implementation-level failures; the isolated TLS failure limited one full-suite validation attempt but did not block the requested test run or explain the five failures.
